title: Fixed-site conditioning gives bilateral count scores of 1.28 and 0.70 in two adult worm maps
abstract: We tested whether low bilateral synapse-count variation remains after fixing release-site budgets in eight C. elegans nerve-ring maps. A new conditional reference moves complete site target sets between source homologs. It fixes site counts on each side and, in the stricter model, within each full site degree. Direct draws retain polyadic target dependence. At 16 or more pooled contacts, the strict mean squared residual score was 1.282 in adult map 7 and 0.699 in adult map 8, against an exact reference mean of 1. Their pointwise 95 percent reference ranges were 0.705 to 1.360 and 0.726 to 1.331. Equal-side binomial scores on the same channels were 0.722 and 0.510. Removing any single source pair preserved both score signs relative to 1. The low adult score did not pass correction for seven maps. The pooled strict score was 0.839 for 287 strong channels (lower rank 0.0311). These results show that low Poisson count scores do not imply uniformly low target-allocation variation under fixed-site budgets. Conditional exchangeability, spatial geometry, annotation, partial coverage and only two adults limit inference. The package supplies original code, exact moments, validation, aggregate results and source hashes. External records are not bundled.
